steps.say: The opening has three simple rules. Rule one: take the center. These four squares are the best real estate on the board.

task.prompt: Play a first move that fights for the center.

feedback.e2e3: That's playable, but push a center pawn two squares to really grab the middle.
feedback.d2d3: That's playable, but push a center pawn two squares to really grab the middle.
feedback.g2g3: That gets your bishop ready, but the center comes first.
feedback.c2c3: That's a quiet start. Grab the center with a pawn two squares forward.
feedback.a2a4: Edge pawns don't help in the middle. Try a center pawn.
feedback.h2h4: Edge pawns don't help in the middle. Try a center pawn.
feedback.g1h3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the middle.
feedback.b1a3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the middle.

task.hint: Push one of the middle pawns two squares.
task.success: Great start! You grab space and open lines for your pieces.

steps.say: Rule two: bring out your knights and bishops. Every move, a new piece joins the game.

task.prompt: Bring out a knight or a bishop. Bonus points if it attacks something.

feedback.g1e2: That develops, but on e2 the knight blocks your bishop. f3 is a better home.
feedback.f1e2: That works, but the bishop does more on c4 or b5.
feedback.f1d3: On d3 the bishop blocks your d-pawn. Find a square with open lines.
feedback.f1a6: The b7 pawn would take it. Green light!
feedback.g1h3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the middle.
feedback.b1a3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the middle.
feedback.d1h5: That's the queen, not a knight or bishop. Early queens get chased.

task.hint: Which knight can jump out and attack the e5 pawn?
task.success: Nicely developed. Every piece you bring out makes your army stronger.

steps.say: Rule three: castle early. It tucks your king into the corner and brings a rook toward the middle.

task.hint: Move your king two squares toward the rook on h1.

steps.say: Why not bring the queen out early? Watch. Black's queen took on d5, and White's knight comes out with an attack.
Now Black has to spend a move running away, while White brings out another piece. Early queens get chased.

task.prompt: Which move follows the opening rules?

options.why: It develops a piece and aims at f7.
Edge pawn moves don't develop anything. Bring out a piece.
Too early for the queen, and she blocks your bishop.

steps.say: Center, develop, castle. Follow those three, and you'll get a good game every time.
